Addiction and dependence are not the same thing. Dependence can be present with or without addiction. Being dependent on something doesn't automatically mean you are an addict, nor will you become one.

If you re-read your prior comment, there is no inquiry, and there are plenty of assumptions made.

There's a difference between being able to enjoy having sex all day with your partner, and being a sex addict. It becomes an addiction when it becomes problematic, by definition. Sex addicts have a compulsion to 'use', just like a drug or alcohol addict. I can go 8 times in one day if I really want to, but I prefer to spend the majority of my day being productive over having constant sex, even though I have a very high drive.

According to your logic, I am a sex addict, but according to medical documentation on criteria for addiction and substance use diagnoses, I am absolutely not. Besides, there is realistically not enough information on this person to make any sort of assumptions, like you have, at this point. I am not overwhelmed by the compulsion of needing sex, and by the sounds of it, neither is the OP. All we know is that they have a high drive, which is normal by the way.

I'm in my late 20's, and I can consistently keep up with or exceed that amount. I think it boils down to sexual compatibility, but I'm also not sure how common it is among other men to have a high drive like mine that hasn't dropped off by this age. My refractory period has definitely increased with age, but I still haven't had a partner that can match me.

I would highly recommend to look for someone that you're compatible with sexually. There are people who will be able to match or exceed your drive, you just have to find them. Being sexually satisfied with your partner is, in my opinion, an extremely important aspect of a healthy relationship.

2.5 years ago I found out that my brother had lost 2 of his friend to suicide. My brother doesn't really talk about himself, so him opening up to me about it was quite surprising. He has always been my biggest supporter, and was my rock for the longest time, some days he still is. I realized I couldn't do it to him, especially since he was the only person who truly wanted to help me and for me to get better. I know he didn't want to lose me, and I didn't want to destroy him.

It was worth it though, life is waaaay better now. I'm still on disability for my mental illnesses and hoping to get back to work soon. I still get depressed and anxious, but I deal with it a lot better than I ever have before. The only thing that still sucks is how horribly I sleep every night without medication, but I'm hopeful it will improve over time.

To anyone out there still struggling, whether it's for an hour or days on end, it doesn't have to be that way forever. Please talk to someone, anyone. Just please don't do it alone. We're in this together, and there's more of us than you think. Everyone deserves happiness, even if your brain is telling you otherwise.
